report.title: Teardown: skill/MCP distribution hubs and their trust mechanics
report.question_or_target: How do the public distribution points for skills and MCP servers (vendor skill repositories, registry/aggregator sites, awesome-lists) establish provenance, review and revocation today, what is the actual review depth, and what would a package need to carry for us to install it automatically?
report.answer: The install-safety conclusion survives but the implement evidence model does not. The four sampled hubs remain discovery/provenance inputs, not standalone automatic-install authorities. Corrected detail: skills.sh does expose content-scoped scanner bindings in its detailed page, though the sampled current skill no longer matches the audited SHA; current MCP policy calls for specific package versions even though a legacy active latest-based record remains. Automatic install still requires verified publisher identity, immutable subject digest, digest-bound review, capability limits, inventory, and version-scoped revocation, all enforced from evidence rather than asserted booleans.

required_package_carriage.must_carry: canonical publisher identity and namespace plus proof of control (GitHub OIDC, DNS/HTTP challenge, or equivalent) and a security contact
required_package_carriage.reject_if: identity is self-asserted, namespace proof is absent, or the contact is missing

required_package_carriage.must_carry: exact version, canonical download URL, SHA-256 (or stronger) artifact digest, source repository, and immutable source commit
required_package_carriage.reject_if: version is latest/main/a range, redirects change origin, digest is absent, or downloaded bytes do not rehash

required_package_carriage.must_carry: signature or transparency-log-verifiable attestation whose subject is the artifact digest, with source/build provenance and builder identity
required_package_carriage.reject_if: signature is absent/invalid, subject digest differs, signer is not policy-allowed, or source-to-artifact correspondence is unproven

required_package_carriage.must_carry: scanner identities/versions/timestamps, findings, human review when risk policy requires it, and every verdict bound to the same subject digest
required_package_carriage.reject_if: any provider reports fail/high/critical, results conflict without adjudication, results are stale, or the reviewed digest differs

required_package_carriage.must_carry: machine-readable tools/commands, filesystem roots, network destinations, secret/environment access, data egress, destructive actions, and required human approvals; undeclared access defaults denied
required_package_carriage.reject_if: capabilities are prose-only, excessive, dynamically undisclosed, or broader at runtime than declared

required_package_carriage.must_carry: license, complete file inventory for prompt-only skills, dependency lock plus SBOM for executable packages, and vulnerability/malware results
required_package_carriage.reject_if: license is incompatible/absent, dependency resolution is mutable, inventory is incomplete, or policy-blocking vulnerabilities remain

required_package_carriage.must_carry: version/digest-scoped status URL or signed feed, status (active/deprecated/revoked), effective timestamp, reason/replacement, update policy, and security advisory channel
required_package_carriage.reject_if: status cannot be refreshed, candidate is not active, advisory scope is ambiguous, or update silently changes the admitted digest

required_package_carriage.must_carry: sandbox profile and local policy mapping; install receipt records all verified evidence and the exact digest
required_package_carriage.reject_if: hub reputation/popularity is substituted for a field, a network check fails closed, or runtime cannot enforce declared boundaries

algorithm: Resolve metadata without executing package code.

Install only in the declared sandbox, record the digest-bound receipt, and poll the revocation feed before every update/use according to risk tier.
